{{judri|section-connected-tenses}}
==Logical and non-logical connections between tenses==
Like many things in Lojban, tenses may be logically connected; logical connection is explained in more detail in 
[[#chapter-connectives|this chapter]]. Some of the terminology in this section will be clear only if you already understand logical connectives.

{{ind|lojban-word-imported|JA selma'o}}  {{ind|general-imported|logically connected tenses|expansion to sentences}}  {{ind|general-imported|tenses|logically connected with JA}}  {{ind|general-imported|logically connected tenses|with JA}} The appropriate logical connectives belong to selma'o JA. A logical connective between tenses can always be expanded to one between sentences:

{{dsp|example-random-id-XAj7}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-XAj7}}
{{judri|c10e20d1}}
:'''mi pu je ba klama le zarci'''
:<code>I [past] and [future] go-to the market.</code>
:''I went and will go to the market.''

means the same as:

{{dsp|example-random-id-BWI5}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-BWI5}}
{{judri|c10e20d2}}
:'''mi pu klama le zarci .ije mi ba klama le zarci'''
:<code>I [past] go-to the market. And I [future] go-to the market.</code>
:''I went to the market, and I will go to the market.''

{{ind|general-imported|tenses|connected|with negation}} Tense connection and tense negation are combined in:

{{dsp|example-random-id-Tuz1}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-Tuz1}}
{{judri|c10e20d3}}
:'''mi punai je canai je ba klama le zarci'''
:<code>I [past] [not] and [present] [not] and [future] go-to the market.</code>
:''I haven't yet gone to the market, but I will in future.''

{{linker|example-random-id-Tuz1}} is far more specific than

{{dsp|example-random-id-J5jJ}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-J5jJ}}
{{judri|c10e20d4}}
:'''mi ba klama le zarci'''
:<code>I [future] go-to the market.</code>

which only says that I will go, without claiming anything about my past or present. 
{{vla|ba}} does not imply 
:{{jbo|punai}} or 
:{{jbo|canai}}; to compel that interpretation, either a logical connection or a ZAhO is needed.

{{ind|general-imported|connected tenses|negation of compared with negation in connective}} Tense negation can often be removed in favor of negation in the logical connective itself. The following examples are equivalent in meaning:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qErC}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qErC}}
{{judri|c10e20d5}}
:'''mi mo'izu'anai je mo'iri'u cadzu'''
:<code>I [motion] [left-not] and [motion] [right] walk.</code>
:''I walk not leftward but rightward.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qeRL}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qeRL}}
{{judri|c10e20d6}}
:'''mi mo'izu'a naje mo'iri'u cadzu'''
:<code>I [motion] [left] not-and [motion] [right] walk.</code>
:''I walk not leftward but rightward.''

{{ind|general-imported|tenses|possible groupings of}}  {{ind|general-imported|tenses|forethought logical connections}} There are no forethought logical connections between tenses allowed by the grammar, to keep tenses simpler. Nor is there any way to override simple left-grouping of the connectives, the Lojban default.

{{ind|lojban-word-imported|GAhO selma'o}}  {{ind|lojban-word-imported|JOI selma'o}}  {{ind|general-imported|intervals|expressing by endpoints with bi'o}}  {{ind|general-imported|tenses|non-logical connection of}} The non-logical connectives of selma'o JOI, BIhI, and GAhO are also permitted between tenses. One application is to specify intervals not by size, but by their end-points ( 
{{vla|bi'o}} belongs to selma'o BIhI, and connects the end-points of an ordered interval, like English 
“from ... to”):

{{dsp|example-random-id-KQUM}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-KQUM}}
{{judri|c10e20d7}}
:'''mi puza bi'o bazu vasxu'''
:<code>I [past] [medium] from ... to [future] [long] breathe.</code>
:''I breathe from a medium time ago till a long time to come.''

(It is to be hoped that I have a long life ahead of me.)

One additional use of non-logical connectives within tenses is discussed in 
[[#section-sub-events|this section]]. Other uses will probably be identified in future.

{{judri|section-sub-events}}
==Sub-events==

{{ind|general-imported|tenses|non-logical connection of for sub-events}} Another application of non-logical tense connection is to talk about sub-events of events. Consider a six-shooter: a gun which can fire six bullets in succession before reloading. If I fire off the entire magazine twice, I can express the fact in Lojban thus:

{{dsp|example-random-id-9CqG}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-9CqG}}
{{judri|c10e21d1}}
{{ind|example|six-shooter|example}}
{{ind|example|on two occasions|example}}
:'''mi reroi pi'u xaroi cecla le seldanti'''
:<code>I [twice] [cross-product] [six times] shoot the projectile-launcher.</code>
:''On two occasions, I fire the gun six times.''

{{ind|general-imported|cross product|with tenses}}  {{ind|general-imported|Cartesian product|with tenses}}  {{ind|general-imported|pi'u|use in connecting tenses}} It would be confusing, though grammatical, to run the 
{{vla|reroi}} and the 
:{{jbo|xaroi}} directly together. However, the non-logical connective 
{{vla|pi'u}} expresses a Cartesian product (also known as a cross product) of two sets. In this case, there is a set of two firings each of which is represented by a set of six shots, for twelve shots in all (hence the name “product”: the product of 2 and 6 is 12). Its use specifies very precisely what occurs.

{{ind|general-imported|event contours|strings of}}  {{ind|general-imported|interval properties|strings of}} In fact, you can specify strings of interval properties and event contours within a single tense without the use of a logical or non-logical connective cmavo. This allows tenses of the type:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qES9}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qES9}}
{{judri|c10e21d2}}
:'''la djordj. ca'o co'a ciska'''
:<code>George [continuitive] [initiative] writes.</code>
:''George continues to start to write.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qetE}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qetE}}
{{judri|c10e21d3}}
:'''mi reroi ca'o xaroi darxi le damri'''
:<code>I [twice] [continuitive] [six times] hit the drum.</code>
:''On two occasions, I continue to beat the drum six times.''

{{judri|section-jai}}
==Conversion of sumti tcita: JAI==
The following cmavo are discussed in this section:

<tabledata class="wikitable">
'''jai'''	JAI	''tense conversion''
'''fai'''	FA	''indefinite place''
</tabledata>

{{ind|lojban-word-imported|SE selma'o}}  {{ind|general-imported|conversion|definition}} Conversion is the regular Lojban process of moving around the places of a place structure. The cmavo of selma'o SE serve this purpose, exchanging the first place with one of the others:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEu5}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEu5}}
{{judri|c10e22d1}}
:'''mi cu klama le zarci'''
:<code>I go-to the market.</code>

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEu9}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEu9}}
{{judri|c10e22d2}}
:'''le zarci cu se klama mi'''
:<code>The market is-gone-to by-me.</code>

{{ind|general-imported|jai with tense|as equivalent of SE in grammar}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense conversion|accessing tense of bridi with jai}}  {{ind|general-imported|conversion|accessing tense of bridi with jai}} It is also possible to bring a place that is specified by a sumti tcita (for the purposes of this chapter, a tense sumti tcita) to the front, by using 
{{vla|jai}} plus the tense as the grammatical equivalent of SE:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEvD}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEvD}}
{{judri|c10e22d3}}
{{ind|example|rat eats cheese in park|example}}
:'''le ratcu cu citka le cirla vi le panka'''
:<code>The rat eats the cheese [short distance] the park.</code>
:''The rat eats the cheese in the park.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEWB}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEWB}}
{{judri|c10e22d4}}
{{ind|example|rat eats cheese in park|example}}
:'''le panka cu jai vi citka le cirla fai le ratcu'''
:<code>The park is-the-place-of eating the cheese by-the rat.</code>
:''The park is where the rat eats the cheese.''

{{ind|general-imported|tense conversion|accessing original first place with fai}} In 
{{linker|example-random-id-qEWB}}, the construction JAI+tense converts the location sumti into the first place. The previous first place has nowhere to go, since the location sumti is not a numbered place; however, it can be inserted back into the bridi with 
{{vla|fai}}, the indefinite member of selma'o FA.

(The other members of FA are used to mark the first, second, etc. places of a bridi explicitly:

{{dsp|example-random-id-YS3i}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-YS3i}}
{{judri|c10e22d5}}
:'''fa mi cu klama fe le zarci'''

means the same as

{{dsp|example-random-id-4DGL}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-4DGL}}
{{judri|c10e22d6}}
:'''fe le zarci cu klama fa mi'''

as well as the simple

{{dsp|example-random-id-Q6J9}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-Q6J9}}
{{judri|c10e22d7}}
:'''mi cu klama le zarci'''

in which the place structure is determined by position.)

{{ind|lojban-word-imported|LE selma'o}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense conversion|use in sumti descriptions}} Like SE conversion, JAI+tense conversion is especially useful in descriptions with LE selma'o:

{{dsp|example-random-id-esDa}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-esDa}}
{{judri|c10e22d8}}
{{ind|example|place of eating|example}}
:'''mi viska le jai vi citka be le cirla'''
:<code>I saw the place-of eating the cheese.</code>

Here the eater of the cheese is elided, so no 
{{vla|fai}} appears.

{{ind|general-imported|tense conversion|of temporal tenses}} Of course, temporal tenses are also usable with JAI:

{{dsp|example-random-id-nSnh}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-nSnh}}
{{judri|c10e22d9}}
:'''mi djuno fi le jai ca morsi be fai la djan.'''
<code>I know about the [present] is-dead of-the-one-called 
“John”.</code>
:<code>I know the time of John's death.</code>
:''I know when John died.''

{{judri|section-tenses-vs-modals}}
==Tenses versus modals==
{{ind|general-imported|modals|contrasted with tenses in semantics}}  {{ind|general-imported|tenses|contrasted with modals in semantics}}  {{ind|general-imported|modals|compared with tenses in syntax}}  {{ind|general-imported|tenses|compared with modals in syntax}} Grammatically, every use of tenses seen so far is exactly paralleled by some use of modals as explained in 
[[#chapter-sumti-tcita|this chapter]]. Modals and tenses alike can be followed by sumti, can appear before the selbri, can be used in pure and mixed connections, can participate in JAI conversions. The parallelism is perfect. However, there is a deep difference in the semantics of tense constructs and modal constructs, grounded in historical differences between the two forms. Originally, modals and tenses were utterly different things in earlier versions of Loglan; only in Lojban have they become grammatically interchangeable. And even now, differences in semantics continue to be maintained.

{{ind|general-imported|modals|importance of 1st sumti place for sumti tcita use}} The core distinction is that whereas the modal bridi

{{dsp|example-random-id-YLmV}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-YLmV}}
{{judri|c10e23d1}}
:'''mi nelci do mu'i le nu do nelci mi'''
:<code>I like you with-motivation the event-of you like me.</code>
:''I like you because you like me.''

places the 
:{{jbo|le nu}} sumti in the x1 place of the gismu 
{{vla|mukti}} (which underlies the modal 
{{vla|mu'i}}), namely the motivating event, the tensed bridi

{{dsp|example-random-id-zXi8}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-zXi8}}
{{judri|c10e23d2}}
:'''mi nelci do ba le nu do nelci mi'''
:<code>I like you after the event-of you like me.</code>
:''I like you after you like me.''

{{ind|general-imported|tenses|importance of 2nd sumti place for sumti tcita use}} places the 
:{{jbo|le nu}} sumti in the x2 place of the gismu 
{{vla|balvi}} (which underlies the tense 
{{vla|ba}}), namely the point of reference for the future tense. Paraphrases of 
{{linker|example-random-id-YLmV}} and 
{{linker|example-random-id-zXi8}}, employing the brivla 
{{vla|mukti}} and 
{{vla|balvi}} explicitly, would be:

{{dsp|example-random-id-JbEU}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-JbEU}}
{{judri|c10e23d3}}
:'''le nu do nelci mi cu mukti le nu mi nelci do'''
:<code>The event-of you like me motivates the event-of I like you.</code>
:''Your liking me is the motive for my liking you.''

and

{{dsp|example-random-id-8sjA}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-8sjA}}
{{judri|c10e23d4}}
:'''le nu mi nelci do cu balvi le nu do nelci mi'''
:<code>The event-of I like you is after the event of you like me.</code>
:''My liking you follows (in time) your liking me.''

(Note that the paraphrase is not perfect due to the difference in what is claimed; 
{{linker|example-random-id-JbEU}} and 
{{linker|example-random-id-8sjA}} claim only the causal and temporal relationships between the events, not the existence of the events themselves.)

{{ind|general-imported|afterthought sentence connection|modal contrasted with tense}} As a result, the afterthought sentence-connective forms of 
{{linker|example-random-id-YLmV}} and 
{{linker|example-random-id-zXi8}} are, respectively:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qewe}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qewe}}
{{judri|c10e23d5}}
:'''mi nelci do .imu'ibo do nelci mi'''
:<code>I like you. [That is] Because you like me.</code>

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEWp}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEWp}}
{{judri|c10e23d6}}
:'''do nelci mi .ibabo mi nelci do'''
:''You like me. Afterward, I like you.''

In 
{{linker|example-random-id-qewe}}, the order of the two bridi 
:{{jbo|mi nelci do}} and 
:{{jbo|do nelci mi}} is the same as in 
{{linker|example-random-id-YLmV}}. In 
{{linker|example-random-id-qEWp}}, however, the order is reversed: the origin point 
:{{jbo|do nelci mi}} physically appears before the future-time event 
:{{jbo|mi nelci do}}. In both cases, the bridi characterizing the event in the x2 place appears before the bridi characterizing the event in the x1 place of 
{{vla|mukti}} or 
{{vla|balvi}}.

{{ind|general-imported|afterthought tense connection|contrasted with forethought in likeness to modal connection}}  {{ind|general-imported|forethought tense connection|contrasted with afterthought in likeness to modal connection}}  {{ind|general-imported|forethought connections|modal compared with tense in semantics}} In forethought connections, however, the asymmetry between modals and tenses is not found. The forethought equivalents of 

{{linker|example-random-id-qewe}} and 
{{linker|example-random-id-qEWp}} are

{{dsp|example-random-id-ENKj}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-ENKj}}
{{judri|c10e23d7}}
:'''mu'igi do nelci mi gi mi nelci do'''
:''Because you like me, I like you.''

and

{{dsp|example-random-id-r7KK}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-r7KK}}
{{judri|c10e23d8}}
:'''bagi do nelci mi gi mi nelci do'''
:''After you like me, I like you.''

respectively.

{{ind|general-imported|modal sentence connection|table of equivalent schemata}} The following modal sentence schemata (where X and Y represent sentences) all have the same meaning:


:'''{{grammar|X .i BAI bo Y}}'''
:'''{{grammar|BAI gi Y gi X}}'''
:'''{{grammar|X BAI le nu Y}}'''
{{ind|general-imported|tense sentence connection|table of equivalent schemata}} whereas the following tensed sentence schemata also have the same meaning:

:'''{{grammar|X .i TENSE bo Y}}'''
:'''{{grammar|TENSE gi X gi Y}}'''
:'''{{grammar|Y TENSE le nu X}}'''
neglecting the question of what is claimed. In the modal sentence schemata, the modal tag is always followed by Y, the sentence representing the event in the x1 place of the gismu that underlies the BAI. In the tensed sentences, no such simple rule exists.

{{judri|section-tense-questions}}
==Tense questions: {{vla|cu'e}}==
The following cmavo is discussed in this section:

<tabledata class="wikitable">
'''cu'e'''	CUhE	''tense question''
</tabledata>

{{ind|general-imported|ma|for tense questions}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense questions with ma}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense questions|methods of asking}} There are two main ways to ask questions about tense. The main English tense question words are 
“When?” and 
“Where?”. These may be paraphrased respectively as 
“At what time?” and 
“At what place?” In these forms, their Lojban equivalents simply involve a tense plus 
{{vla|ma}}, the Lojban sumti question:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEwW}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEwW}}
{{judri|c10e24d1}}
{{ind|example|when|example}}
:'''do klama le zdani ca ma'''
:<code>You go-to the house [present] [what sumti?].</code>
:<code>You go to the house at what time?</code>
:''When do you go to the house?''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEX2}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEX2}}
{{judri|c10e24d2}}
{{ind|example|where|example}}
:'''le verba vi ma pu cadzu le bisli'''
:<code>The child [short space] [what sumti?] [past] walks-on the ice.</code>
:<code>The child at/near what place walked on the ice?</code>
:''Where did the child walk on the ice?''

{{ind|general-imported|modal-or-tense question|with cu'e}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense-or-modal questions|with cu'e}} There is also a non-specific tense and modal question, 
{{vla|cu'e}}, belonging to selma'o CUhE. This can be used wherever a tense or modal construct can be used.

{{dsp|example-random-id-4dAJ}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-4dAJ}}
{{judri|c10e24d3}}
{{ind|example|when/where/how|example}}
:'''le nanmu cu'e batci le gerku'''
:<code>The man [what tense?] bites the dog.</code>
:''When/Where/How does the man bite the dog?''

{{ind|general-imported|answers|to tense-or-modal questions}} Possible answers to 
{{linker|example-random-id-4dAJ}} might be:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qeya}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qeya}}
{{judri|c10e24d4}}
:'''va'''
:<code>[medium space].</code>
:''Some ways from here.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEYe}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEYe}}
{{judri|c10e24d5}}
:'''puzu'''
:<code>[past] [long time].</code>
:''A long time ago.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qEyQ}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qEyQ}}
{{judri|c10e24d6}}
:'''vi le lunra'''
:<code>[short space] The moon.</code>
:''On the moon.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qez6}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qez6}}
{{judri|c10e24d7}}
:'''pu'o'''
:<code>[inchoative]</code>
:''He hasn't yet done so.''

or even the modal reply (from selma'o BAI; See [[#section-BAI|this section]]):

{{dsp|example-random-id-Vqgy}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-Vqgy}}
{{judri|c10e24d8}}
:'''seka'a le briju'''
:<code>With-destination the office.</code>

{{ind|general-imported|modal-or-tense questions|pre-specifying some information}}  {{ind|general-imported|tense-or-modal questions|pre-specifying some information}}  {{ind|general-imported|cu'e|combining with other tense cmavo}} The only way to combine 
{{vla|cu'e}} with other tense cmavo is through logical connection, which makes a question that pre-specifies some information:

{{dsp|example-random-id-QTts}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-QTts}}
{{judri|c10e24d9}}
{{ind|example|when else|example}}
{{ind|example|sowed grain|example}}
:'''do puzi je cu'e sombo le gurni'''
:<code>You [past] [short] and [when?] sow the grain?</code>
:''You sowed the grain a little while ago; when else do you sow it?''

Additionally, the logical connective itself can be replaced by a question word:

{{ind|general-imported|tense questions|by using logical connective question}}

{{dsp|example-random-id-I6xI}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-I6xI}}
{{judri|c10e24d10}}
:'''la .artr. pu je'i ba nolraitru'''
:<code>Arthur [past] [which?] [future] is-a-king</code>
:''Was Arthur a king or will he be?''

Answers to 
{{linker|example-random-id-I6xI}} would be logical connectives such as 
{{vla|je}}, meaning 
“both”, 
:{{jbo|naje}} meaning 
“the latter”, or 
{{vla|jenai}} meaning 
“the former”.

{{judri|section-explicit-magnitudes}}
==Explicit magnitudes==
It is a limitation of the VA and ZI system of specifying magnitudes that they can only prescribe vague magnitudes: small, medium, or large. In order to express both an origin point and an exact distance, the Lojban construction called a “termset” is employed. (Termsets are explained further in 
[[#section-termsets|this section]] and 
[[#section-quantifier-grouping|this section]].) It is grammatical for a termset to be placed after a tense or modal tag rather than a sumti, which allows both the origin of the imaginary journey and its distance to be specified. Here is an example:

{{dsp|example-random-id-7Lys}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-7Lys}}
{{judri|c10e25d1}}
:'''la frank. sanli zu'a nu'i la djordj. la'u lo mitre be li mu [nu'u]'''
:<code>Frank stands [left] [start termset] George [quantity] a thing-measuring-in-meters the-number 5 [end termset].</code>
:''Frank is standing five meters to the left of George.''

Here the termset extends from the 
{{vla|nu'i}} to the implicit 
{{vla|nu'u}} at the end of the sentence, and includes the terms 
:{{jbo|la djordj.}}, which is the unmarked origin point, and the tagged sumti 
:{{jbo|lo mitre be li mu}}, which the cmavo 
{{vla|la'u}} (of selma'o BAI, and meaning 
“with quantity”; See [[#section-BAI|this section]]) marks as a quantity. Both terms are governed by the tag 
{{vla|zu'a}}
It is not necessary to have both an origin point and an explicit magnitude: a termset may have only a single term in it. A less precise version of 

{{linker|example-random-id-7Lys}} is:

{{dsp|example-random-id-RWEE}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-RWEE}}
{{judri|c10e25d2}}
:'''la frank. sanli zu'a nu'i la'u lo mitre be li mu'''
:<code>Frank stands [left] [termset] [quantity] a thing-measuring-in-meters the-number 5.</code>
:''Frank stands five meters to the left.''

{{judri|section-exercise}}
==Finally (an exercise for the much-tried reader)==

{{dsp|example-random-id-NxGB}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-NxGB}}
{{judri|c10e26d1}}
:'''.a'o do pu seju ba roroi ca'o fe'e su'oroi jimpe fi le lojbo temci selsku ciste'''

{{judri|section-tense-selmaho-summary}}
==Summary of tense selma'o==
{{ind|general-imported|tense selma'o|summary of}}

<tabledata class="wikitable">
'''PU'''	temporal direction''
	pu = past, ca = present, ba = future''

'''ZI'''	temporal distance''
	zi = short, za = medium, zu = long''

'''ZEhA'''	temporal interval''
	ze'i = short, ze'a = medium, ze'u = long, ze'e = infinite''

'''ROI'''	objective quantified tense flag''
	noroi = never, paroi = once, ..., roroi = always, etc.''
	pare'u = the first time, rere'u = the second time, etc.''

'''TAhE'''	subjective quantified tense''
	di'i = regularly, na'o = typically, ru'i = continuously, ta'e = habitually''

'''ZAhO'''	event contours''
	see Section 10''

'''FAhA'''	spatial direction''
	see Section 28''

'''VA'''	spatial distance''
	vi = short, va = medium, vu = long''

'''VEhA'''	spatial interval''
	ve'i = short, ve'a = medium, ve'u = long, ve'e = infinite''

'''VIhA'''	spatial dimensionality''
	vi'i = line, vi'a = plane, vi'u = space, vi'e = space-time''

'''FEhE'''	spatial interval modifier flag''
	fe'enoroi = nowhere, fe'eroroi = everywhere, fe'eba'o = beyond, etc.''

'''MOhI'''	spatial movement flag''
	mo'i = motion; see Section 28''

'''KI'''	set or reset sticky tense''
	tense+“ki” = set, “ki” alone = reset''

'''CUhE'''	tense question, reference point''
	cu'e = asks for a tense or aspect, nau = use speaker’s reference point''

'''JAI'''	tense conversion''
	jaica = the time of, jaivi = the place of, etc.''
</tabledata>


{{judri|section-direction-cmavo}}
==List of spatial directions and direction-like relations==

{{vla|mo'i}} to express a direction, and then when used with 
{{vla|mo'i}} to express movement in the direction. When possible, the gismu from which the cmavo is derived is also listed.

{{ind|general-imported|ze'o|special note on direction orientation}}  {{ind|general-imported|zo'i|special note on direction orientation}}  {{ind|general-imported|to'o|special note on direction orientation}}  {{ind|general-imported|fa'a|special note on direction orientation}} Special note on 
{{vla|fa'a}}, 
{{vla|to'o}}, 
{{vla|zo'i}}, and 
{{vla|ze'o}}:

{{vla|zo'i}} and 
{{vla|ze'o}} refer to direction towards or away from the speaker's location, or whatever the origin is.

{{vla|fa'a}} and 
{{vla|to'o}} refer to direction towards or away from some other point.

{{startchapter|{{#var:uni}}}}{{judri|chapter-abstractions}}
=Events, Qualities, Quantities, And Other Vague Words: On Lojban Abstraction=
{{image|xml:id="chapter-abstractions-picture"|The picture for chapter 11|media/chapter-abstractions.gif}}
{{judri|section-syntax}}
==The syntax of abstraction==
The purpose of the feature of Lojban known as 
“abstraction” is to provide a means for taking whole bridi and packaging them up, as it were, into simple selbri. Syntactically, abstractions are very simple and uniform; semantically, they are rich and complex, with few features in common between one variety of abstraction and another. We will begin by discussing syntax without regard to semantics; as a result, the notion of abstraction may seem unmotivated at first. Bear with this difficulty until 
[[#section-events|this section]].

An abstraction selbri is formed by taking a full bridi and preceding it by any cmavo of selma'o NU. There are twelve such cmavo; they are known as 
“abstractors”. The bridi is closed by the elidable terminator 
{{vla|kei}}, of selma'o KEI. Thus, to change the bridi

{{dsp|example-random-id-6EI1}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-6EI1}}
{{judri|c11e1d1}}
:'''mi klama le zarci'''
:<code>I go-to the store</code>

into an abstraction using 
{{vla|nu}}, one of the members of selma'o NU, we change it into

{{dsp|example-random-id-Via0}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-Via0}}
{{judri|c11e1d2}}
:'''nu mi klama le zarci [kei]'''
:<code>an-event-of my going-to the store</code>

{{ind|general-imported|KEI selma'o|eliding}}  {{ind|general-imported|observatives|and abstractions}} The bridi may be a simple selbri, or it may have associated sumti, as here. It is important to beware of eliding 
{{vla|kei}} improperly, as many of the common uses of abstraction selbri involve following them with words that would appear to be part of the abstraction if 
{{vla|kei}} had been elided.

(Technically, 
{{vla|kei}} is never necessary, because the elidable terminator 
{{vla|vau}} that closes every bridi can substitute for it; however, 
{{vla|kei}} is specific to abstractions, and using it is almost always clearer.)

{{ind|general-imported|tanru|and abstractions}}  {{ind|general-imported|abstractions|grammatical uses}} The grammatical uses of an abstraction selbri are exactly the same as those of a simple brivla. In particular, abstraction selbri may be used as observatives, as in 

{{linker|example-random-id-Via0}}, or used in tanru:

{{dsp|example-random-id-0Ff4}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-0Ff4}}
{{judri|c11e1d3}}
{{ind|example|want to be a soldier|example}}
:'''la djan. cu nu sonci kei djica'''
:<code>John is-an-(event-of being-a-soldier) type-of desirer.</code>
:''John wants to be a soldier.''

{{ind|general-imported|descriptions|and abstractions}} Abstraction selbri may also be used in descriptions, preceded by 
{{vla|le}} (or any other member of selma'o LE):

{{dsp|example-random-id-sQ33}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-sQ33}}
{{judri|c11e1d4}}
:'''la djan. cu djica le nu sonci [kei]'''
:<code>John desires the event-of being-a-soldier.</code>

We will most often use descriptions containing abstraction either at the end of a bridi, or just before the main selbri with its 
{{vla|cu}}; in either of these circumstances, 
{{vla|kei}} can normally be elided.

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|place structure}} The place structure of an abstraction selbri depends on the particular abstractor, and will be explained individually in the following sections.

Note: In glosses of bridi within abstractions, the grammatical form used in the English changes. Thus, in the gloss of 
{{linker|example-random-id-Via0}} we see 
“my going-to the store” rather than 
“I go-to the store”; likewise, in the glosses of 
{{linker|example-random-id-0Ff4}} and 
{{linker|example-random-id-sQ33}} we see 
“being-a-soldier” rather than 
“is-a-soldier”. This procedure reflects the desire for more understandable glosses, and does not indicate any change in the Lojban form. A bridi is a bridi, and undergoes no change when it is used as part of an abstraction selbri.

{{judri|section-events}}
==Event abstraction==
{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|event}}  {{ind|general-imported|event abstractions}} The following cmavo is discussed in this section:

<tabledata class="wikitable">
'''nu'''	NU	''event abstractor''
</tabledata>

{{ind|general-imported|le nu|definition}}  {{ind|general-imported|nu|definition}}  {{ind|general-imported|common abstractor}} The examples in 
[[#section-syntax|this section]] made use of 
{{vla|nu}} as the abstractor, and it is certainly the most common abstractor in Lojban text. Its purpose is to capture the event or state of the bridi considered as a whole. Do not confuse the 

{{vla|le}} description built on a 
{{vla|nu}} abstraction with ordinary descriptions based on 
{{vla|le}} alone. The following sumti are quite distinct:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qF0u}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qF0u}}
{{judri|c11e2d1}}
:'''le klama'''
:''the comer, that which comes''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qF0U}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qF0U}}
{{judri|c11e2d2}}
:'''le se klama'''
:''the destination''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qf11}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qf11}}
{{judri|c11e2d3}}
:'''le te klama'''
:''the origin''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qf22}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qf22}}
{{judri|c11e2d4}}
:'''le ve klama'''
:''the route''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qf4x}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qf4x}}
{{judri|c11e2d5}}
:'''le xe klama'''
:''the means of transportation''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qf97}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qf97}}
{{judri|c11e2d6}}
:'''le nu klama'''
:''the event of someone coming to somewhere from somewhere by some route using some means''

{{linker|example-random-id-qF0u}} through 
{{linker|example-random-id-qf4x}} are descriptions that isolate the five individual sumti places of the selbri 
{{vla|klama}}. 
{{linker|example-random-id-qf97}} describes something associated with the bridi as a whole: the event of it.

{{ind|general-imported|events|duration}} In Lojban, the term 
“event” is divorced from its ordinary English sense of something that happens over a short period of time. The description:

{{dsp|example-random-id-mxAt}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-mxAt}}
{{judri|c11e2d7}}
:'''le nu mi vasxu'''
:<code>the event-of my breathing</code>

is an event which lasts for the whole of my life (under normal circumstances). On the other hand,

{{dsp|example-random-id-BPcI}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-BPcI}}
{{judri|c11e2d8}}
{{ind|example|kissing Jane|example}}
:'''le nu la djan. cinba la djein.'''
:<code>the event-of John kissing Jane</code>

{{ind|general-imported|normal circumstances}} is relatively brief by comparison (again, under normal circumstances).

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|sumti ellipsis in}} We can see from 
{{linker|example-random-id-qf97}} through 
{{linker|example-random-id-BPcI}} that ellipsis of sumti is valid in the bridi of abstraction selbri, just as in the main bridi of a sentence. Any sumti may be ellipsized if the listener will be able to figure out from context what the proper value of it is, or else to recognize that the proper value is unimportant. It is extremely common for 

{{vla|nu}} abstractions in descriptions to have the x1 place ellipsized:

{{dsp|example-random-id-FRoP}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-FRoP}}
{{judri|c11e2d9}}
:'''mi nelci le nu limna'''
:<code>I like the event-of swimming.</code>
:''I like swimming.''

is elliptical, and most probably means:

{{dsp|example-random-id-Ys8w}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-Ys8w}}
{{judri|c11e2d10}}
:'''mi nelci le nu mi limna'''
:<code>I like the event-of I swim.</code>

In the proper context, of course, 
{{linker|example-random-id-FRoP}} could refer to the event of somebody else swimming. Its English equivalent, 
“I like swimming”, can't be interpreted as 
“I like Frank's swimming”; this is a fundamental distinction between English and Lojban. In Lojban, an omitted sumti can mean whatever the context indicates that it should mean.

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|implicit in sumti}} Note that the lack of an explicit NU cmavo in a sumti can sometimes hide an implicit abstraction. In the context of 
{{linker|example-random-id-Ys8w}}, the appearance of 
:{{jbo|le se nelci}} ( 
“that which is liked”) is in effect an abstraction:

{{dsp|example-random-id-sMsx}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-sMsx}}
{{judri|c11e2d11}}
:'''le se nelci cu cafne'''
:<code>The liked-thing is-frequent.</code>
:''The thing which I like happens often.''

which in this context means

:''My swimming happens often.''
Event descriptions with 
:{{jbo|le nu}} are commonly used to fill the 
“under conditions...” places, among others, of gismu and lujvo place structures:

{{dsp|example-random-id-Ia6f}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-Ia6f}}
{{judri|c11e2d12}}
{{ind|example|under conditions|example}}
:'''la lojban. cu frili mi le nu mi tadni [kei]'''
:<code>Lojban is-easy for-me under-conditions-the event-of I study</code>
:''Lojban is easy for me when I study.''

(The “when” of the English would also be appropriate for a construction involving a Lojban tense, but the Lojban sentence says more than that the studying is concurrent with the ease.)

{{ind|general-imported|nu|place structure}}  {{ind|general-imported|events|place structure}} The place structure of a 
{{vla|nu}} abstraction selbri is simply:

:''x1 is an event of (the bridi)''

{{judri|section-event-types}}
==Types of event abstractions==

{{ind|general-imported|event abstractions|types}} The following cmavo are discussed in this section:

<tabledata class="wikitable">
'''mu'e'''	NU	''point-event abstractor''
'''pu'u'''	NU	''process abstractor''
'''zu'o'''	NU	''activity abstractor''
'''za'i'''	NU	''state abstractor''
</tabledata>

Event abstractions with 
{{vla|nu}} suffice to express all kinds of events, whether long, short, unique, repetitive, or whatever. Lojban also has more finely discriminating machinery for talking about events, however. There are four other abstractors of selma'o NU for talking about four specific types of events, or four ways of looking at the same event.

{{ind|general-imported|achievement abstractions|definition}}  {{ind|general-imported|point-event abstractions|definition}}  {{ind|general-imported|abstractions|achievement}}  {{ind|general-imported|abstractions|point-event}}  {{ind|general-imported|triumph}}  {{ind|general-imported|point-event abstractor}} An event considered as a point in time is called a 
“point-event”, or sometimes an 
“achievement”. (This latter word should be divorced, in this context, from all connotations of success or triumph.) A point-event can be extended in duration, but it is still a point-event if it is thought of as unitary, having no internal structure. The abstractor 

{{vla|mu'e}} means 

“point-event-of”:

{{dsp|example-random-id-nFR1}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-nFR1}}
{{judri|c11e3d1}}
{{ind|example|killing Jim|example}}
:'''le mu'e la djan. catra la djim. cu zekri'''
:<code>The point-event-of (John kills Jim) is-a-crime.</code>
:''John's killing Jim (considered as a point in time) is a crime.''

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|process}}  {{ind|general-imported|process abstractions|definition}}  {{ind|general-imported|process abstractor}}  {{ind|general-imported|killing Jim}} An event considered as extended in time, and structured with a beginning, a middle containing one or more stages, and an end, is called a 
“process”. The abstractor 
{{vla|pu'u}} means 

“process-of”:

{{dsp|example-random-id-WaxD}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-WaxD}}
{{judri|c11e3d2}}
{{ind|example|Roman Empire|example}}
:'''ca'o le pu'u le latmo balje'a cu porpi kei so'i je'atru cu selcatra'''
:<code>[continuitive] the process-of( the Latin great-state breaking-up ) many state-rulers were-killed</code>
:''During the fall of the Roman Empire, many Emperors were killed.''

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|activity}}  {{ind|general-imported|activity abstractions|definition}}  {{ind|general-imported|activity abstractor}}  {{ind|general-imported|Roman Empire}} An event considered as extended in time and cyclic or repetitive is called an 
“activity”. The abstractor 
{{vla|zu'o}} means 

“activity-of”:

{{dsp|example-random-id-89nw}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-89nw}}
{{judri|c11e3d3}}
:'''mi tatpi ri'a le zu'o mi plipe'''
:<code>I am-tired because-of the activity-of (I jump).</code>
:''I am tired because I jump.''

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|state}}  {{ind|general-imported|state abstractions|definition}}  {{ind|general-imported|state abstractor}} An event considered as something that is either happening or not happening, with sharp boundaries, is called a 
“state”. The abstractor 
{{vla|za'i}} means 

“state-of”:

{{dsp|example-random-id-WztQ}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-WztQ}}
{{judri|c11e3d4}}
{{ind|example|being alive|example}}
:'''le za'i mi jmive cu ckape do'''
:<code>The state-of (I am-alive) is-dangerous-to you.</code>
:''My being alive is dangerous to you.''

{{ind|general-imported|event types|described}} The abstractors in 
{{linker|example-random-id-nFR1}} through 
{{linker|example-random-id-WztQ}} could all have been replaced by 
{{vla|nu}}, with some loss of precision. Note that Lojban allows every sort of event to be viewed in any of these four ways:
* {{ind|general-imported|state event|described}} the 
“state of running” begins when the runner starts and ends when the runner stops;
* {{ind|general-imported|activity event|described}} the 
“activity of running” consists of the cycle 
“lift leg, step forward, drop leg, lift other leg...” (each such cycle is a process, but the activity consists in the repetition of the cycle);
* {{ind|general-imported|process event|described}}  {{ind|general-imported|slowdown}}  {{ind|general-imported|steady speed}} the 
“process of running” puts emphasis on the initial sprint, the steady speed, and the final slowdown;
* {{ind|general-imported|achievement event|described}}  {{ind|general-imported|Athens}}  {{ind|general-imported|indivisible}}  {{ind|general-imported|marathon}}  {{ind|general-imported|Pheidippides}} the 
“achievement of running” is most alien to English, but sees the event of running as a single indivisible thing, like 

“Pheidippides' run from Marathon to Athens” (the original marathon).

Further information on types of events can be found in 
[[#section-abstractor-connection|this section]].

The four event type abstractors have the following place structures:

<!--
FIXME: put the index entries in

<cx "achievement abstraction: place structure"> XE "achievement abstraction: place structure"

<cx "point-event abstraction: place structure"> XE "point-event abstraction: place structure"

<cx "mu'e: place structure"> XE "mu'e: place structure"

<dt><dd>"mu'e”:  x1 is a point event of (the bridi)

<cx "process abstraction: place structure"> XE "process abstraction: place structure"

<cx "pu'u: place structure"> XE "pu'u: place structure"
"pu'u”:  x1 is a process of (the bridi) with stages x2

<cx "state abstraction: place structure"> XE "state abstraction: place structure"

<cx "za'i: place structure"> XE "za'i: place structure"
"za'i”:  x1 is a continuous state of (the bridi) being true

<cx "activity abstraction: place structure"> XE "activity abstraction: place structure"

<cx "zu'o: place structure"> XE "zu'o: place structure"
"zu'o”:  x1 is an activity of (the bridi) consisting of repeated actions x2

-->

{{vla|mu'e}} :''x1 is a point event of (the bridi)''

{{vla|pu'u}}: x1 is a process of (the bridi) with stages x2

{{vla|za'i}}: x1 is a continuous state of (the bridi) being true

{{vla|zu'o}}: x1 is an activity of (the bridi) consisting of repeated actions x2



{{judri|section-properties}}
==Property abstractions==
The following cmavo are discussed in this section:

<tabledata class="wikitable">
'''ka'''	NU	''property abstractor''
'''ce'u'''	KOhA	''abstraction focus''
</tabledata>
The things described by 
:{{jbo|le nu}} descriptions (or, to put it another way, the things of which 
{{vla|nu}} selbri may correctly be predicated) are only moderately 
“abstract”. They are still closely tied to happenings in space and time. Properties, however, are much more ethereal. What is 
“the property of being blue”, or 
“the property of being a go-er”? They are what logicians call 
“intensions”. If John has a heart, then 

“the property of having a heart” is an abstract object which, when applied to John, is true. In fact,

{{dsp|example-random-id-YSUx}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-YSUx}}
{{judri|c11e4d1}}
{{ind|example|has a heart|example}}
:'''la djan. cu se risna zo'e'''
:<code>John has-as-heart something-unspecified.</code>
:''John has a heart.''

has the same truth conditions as

{{dsp|example-random-id-1PPS}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-1PPS}}
{{judri|c11e4d2}}
:'''la djan. cu ckaji le ka se risna [zo'e] [kei]'''
:<code>John has-the-property the property-of having-as-heart something.</code>
:''John has the property of having a heart.''

{{ind|general-imported|having|of properties}} (The English word 
“have” frequently appears in any discussion of Lojban properties: things are said to 
“have” properties, but this is not the same sense of 
“have” as in 
“I have money”, which is possession.)

Property descriptions, like event descriptions, are often wanted to fill places in brivla place structures:

{{dsp|example-random-id-v3Ba}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-v3Ba}}
{{judri|c11e4d3}}
:'''do cnino mi le ka xunre [kei]'''
:<code>You are-new to-me in-the-quality-of-the property-of being-red.</code>
:''You are new to me in redness.''

{{ind|general-imported|-ity}}  {{ind|general-imported|-ness}} (The English suffix 
“-ness” often signals a property abstraction, as does the suffix “-ity”.)

{{ind|general-imported|property description}} We can also move the property description to the x1 place of 

{{linker|example-random-id-v3Ba}}, producing:

{{dsp|example-random-id-proQ}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-proQ}}
{{judri|c11e4d4}}
:'''le ka do xunre [kei] cu cnino mi'''
:<code>The property-of your being-red is-new to me.</code>
:''Your redness is new to me.''

{{ind|general-imported|beach|example}}  {{ind|general-imported|sunburn|example}} It would be suitable to use 
{{linker|example-random-id-v3Ba}} and 
{{linker|example-random-id-proQ}} to someone who has returned from the beach with a sunburn.

{{ind|general-imported|property abstractions|specifying determining place by sumti ellipsis}}  {{ind|general-imported|property abstractions|sumti ellipsis in}} There are several different properties that can be extracted from a bridi, depending on which place of the bridi is 
“understood” as being specified externally. Thus:

{{dsp|example-random-id-H71J}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-H71J}}
{{judri|c11e4d5}}
{{ind|example|property of loving|example}}
:'''ka mi prami [zo'e] [kei]'''
:<code>a-property-of me loving something-unspecified</code>

is quite different from

{{dsp|example-random-id-wcxY}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-wcxY}}
{{judri|c11e4d6}}
:'''ka [zo'e] prami mi [kei]'''
:<code>a-property-of something-unspecified loving me</code>

In particular, sentences like 
{{linker|example-random-id-qfAM}} and 
{{linker|example-random-id-qfav}} are quite different in meaning:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qfAM}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qfAM}}
{{judri|c11e4d7}}
{{ind|example|love more|example}}
:'''la djan. cu zmadu la djordj. le ka mi prami'''
:<code>John exceeds George in-the property-of (I love X)</code>
:''I love John more than I love George.''

{{dsp|example-random-id-qfav}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qfav}}
{{judri|c11e4d8}}
:'''la djan. cu zmadu la djordj. le ka prami mi'''
:<code>John exceeds George in the property of (X loves me).</code>
:''John loves me more than George loves me.''

{{ind|general-imported|property abstractions|specifying determining place with ce'u}} 

The “X” used in the glosses of 
{{linker|example-random-id-qfAM}} through 
{{linker|example-random-id-qfav}} as a place-holder cannot be represented only by ellipsis in Lojban, because ellipsis means that there must be a specific value that can fill the ellipsis, as mentioned in 

[[#section-events|this section]]. Instead, the cmavo 
{{vla|ce'u}} of selma'o KOhA is employed when an explicit sumti is wanted. (The form 
“X” will be used in literal translations.)

Therefore, an explicit equivalent of 
{{linker|example-random-id-qfAM}}, with no ellipsis, is:

{{dsp|example-random-id-8DD8}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-8DD8}}
{{judri|c11e4d9}}
:'''la djan. cu zmadu la djordj. le ka mi prami ce'u'''
:<code>John exceeds George in-the property-of (I love X).</code>

and of 
{{linker|example-random-id-qfav}} is:

{{dsp|example-random-id-JKBQ}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-JKBQ}}
{{judri|c11e4d10}}
:'''la djan. cu zmadu la djordj. le ka ce'u prami mi'''
:<code>John exceeds George in-the property-of (X loves me).</code>

This convention allows disambiguation of cases like:

{{dsp|example-random-id-GiJp}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-GiJp}}
{{judri|c11e4d11}}
{{ind|example|giving the horse|example}}
:'''le ka [zo'e] dunda le xirma [zo'e] [kei]'''
:<code>the property-of giving the horse</code>
into
{{dsp|example-random-id-1vc4}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-1vc4}}
{{judri|c11e4d12}}
:'''le ka ce'u dunda le xirma [zo'e] [kei]'''
:<code>the property-of (X is-a-giver of-the horse to someone-unspecified)</code>
:''the property of being a giver of the horse''

which is the most natural interpretation of 
{{linker|example-random-id-GiJp}}, versus

{{dsp|example-random-id-rDtg}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-rDtg}}
{{judri|c11e4d13}}
:'''le ka [zo'e] dunda le xirma ce'u [kei]'''
:<code>the property-of (someone-unspecified is-a-giver of-the horse to X)</code>
:''the property of being one to whom the horse is given''
which is also a possible interpretation.

{{ind|general-imported|property abstractions|use of multiple ce'u for relationship abstraction}}  {{ind|general-imported|relationship abstraction}} It is also possible to have more than one 
{{vla|ce'u}} in a 
{{vla|ka}} abstraction, which transforms it from a property abstraction into a relationship abstraction. Relationship abstractions 

“package up” a complex relationship for future use; such an abstraction can be translated back into a selbri by placing it in the x2 place of the selbri 
{{vla|bridi}}, whose place structure is:

{{vla|bridi}} :''x1 is a predicate relationship with relation
x2 (abstraction) among arguments (sequence/set) x3''

{{ind|general-imported|properties|place structure}} The place structure of 
{{vla|ka}} abstraction selbri is simply:

{{vla|ka}} :''x1 is a property of (the bridi)''


{{judri|section-amounts}}
==Amount abstractions==
The following cmavo is discussed in this section:

<tabledata class="wikitable">
'''ni'''	NU	''amount abstraction''
</tabledata>

Amount abstractions are far more limited than event or property abstractions. They really make sense only if the selbri of the abstracted bridi is subject to measurement of some sort. Thus we can speak of:

{{dsp|example-random-id-QW2C}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-QW2C}}
{{judri|c11e5d1}}
:'''le ni le pixra cu blanu [kei]'''
:<code>the amount-of (the picture being-blue)</code>
:''the amount of blueness in the picture''

because “blueness” could be measured with a colorimeter or a similar device. However,

{{dsp|example-random-id-FyL4}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-FyL4}}
{{judri|c11e5d2}}
:'''le ni la djein. cu mamta [kei]'''
:<code>the amount-of (Jane being-a-mother)</code>
:<code>the amount of Jane's mother-ness (?)</code>
:<code>the amount of mother-ness in Jane (?)</code>

makes very little sense in either Lojban or English. We simply do not have any sort of measurement scale for being a mother.

Semantically, a sumti with 
:{{jbo|le ni}} is a number; however, it cannot be treated grammatically as a quantifier in Lojban unless prefixed by the mathematical cmavo 
{{vla|mo'e}}:

{{dsp|example-random-id-SaTi}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-SaTi}}
{{judri|c11e5d3}}
:'''li pa vu'u mo'e le ni le pixra cu blanu [kei]'''
:<code>the-number 1 minus the-operand the amount-of (the picture being-blue)</code>
:''{{math|1 - B}}, where B = blueness of the picture''

Mathematical Lojban is beyond the scope of this chapter, and is explained more fully in 
[[#chapter-mekso|this chapter]].

There are contexts where either property or amount abstractions make sense, and in such constructions, amount abstractions can make use of 
{{vla|ce'u}} just like property abstractors. Thus,

{{dsp|example-random-id-1LtX}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-1LtX}}
{{judri|c11e5d4}}
:'''le pixra cu cenba le ka ce'u blanu [kei]'''
:<code>The picture varies in-the property-of (X is blue).</code>
:<code>The picture varies in being blue.</code>
:''The picture varies in blueness.''

is not the same as

{{dsp|example-random-id-QKpo}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-QKpo}}
{{judri|c11e5d5}}
:'''le pixra cu cenba le ni ce'u blanu [kei]'''
:<code>The picture varies in-the amount-of (X is blue).</code>
:<code>The picture varies in how blue it is.</code>
:''The picture varies in blueness.''

{{linker|example-random-id-1LtX}} conveys that the blueness comes and goes, whereas 
{{linker|example-random-id-QKpo}} conveys that its quantity changes over time.

Whenever we talk of measurement of an amount, there is some sort of scale, and so the place structure of 
{{vla|ni}} abstraction selbri is:

{{vla|ni}} :''x1 is the amount of (the bridi) on scale x2''

Note: the best way to express the x2 places of abstract sumti is to use something like {{jbo|le ni ... kei be}}. See {{linker|example-random-id-zvfX}} for the use of this construction.

{{judri|section-truth-values}}
==Truth-value abstraction: 
{{vla|jei}}==
The “blueness of the picture” discussed in 
[[#section-amounts|this section]] refers to the measurable amount of blue pigment (or other source of blueness), not to the degree of truth of the claim that blueness is present. That abstraction is expressed in Lojban using 
{{vla|jei}}, which is closely related semantically to 
{{vla|ni}}. In the simplest cases, 
:{{jbo|le jei}} produces not a number but a truth value:

{{dsp|example-random-id-KuTE}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-KuTE}}
{{judri|c11e6d1}}
{{ind|example|2 + 2|example}}
:'''le jei li re su'i re du li vo [kei]'''
:<code>the truth-value-of the-number 2 + 2 = the-number 4</code>
:''the truth of 2 + 2 being 4''

is equivalent to “truth”, and

{{dsp|example-random-id-nYY2}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-nYY2}}
{{judri|c11e6d2}}
:'''le jei li re su'i re du li mu [kei]'''
:<code>the truth-value-of the-number 2 + 2 = the-number 5</code>
:''the truth of 2 + 2 being 5''

is equivalent to “falsehood”.

However, not everything in life (or even in Lojban) is simply true or false. There are shades of gray even in truth value, and 
{{vla|jei}} is Lojban's mechanism for indicating the shade of grey intended:

{{dsp|example-random-id-MRD8}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-MRD8}}
{{judri|c11e6d3}}
{{ind|example|whether criminal|example}}
:'''mi ba jdice le jei la djordj. cu zekri gasnu [kei]'''
:<code>I [future] decide the truth-value of (George being-a-(crime doer)).</code>
:''I will decide whether George is a criminal.''

{{ind|general-imported|jei|place structure}}  {{ind|general-imported|truth-value abstractions|place structure}}  {{ind|general-imported|legal system}} 
{{linker|example-random-id-MRD8}} does not imply that George is, or is not, definitely a criminal. Depending on the legal system I am using, I may make some intermediate decision. As a result, 

{{vla|jei}} requires an x2 place analogous to that of 
{{vla|ni}}:

{{vla|jei}} :''x1 is the truth value of (the bridi) under epistemology x2''

{{ind|general-imported|fuzzy logic and truth-value abstraction}}  {{ind|general-imported|abstractions|truth-value and fuzzy logic}} Abstractions using 
{{vla|jei}} are the mechanism for fuzzy logic in Lojban; the 
{{vla|jei}} abstraction refers to a number between 0 and 1 inclusive (as distinct from 
{{vla|ni}} abstractions, which are often on open-ended scales). The detailed conventions for using 
{{vla|jei}} in fuzzy-logic contexts have not yet been established.

{{judri|section-predications}}
==Predication/sentence abstraction==

The following cmavo is discussed in this section:

<tabledata class="wikitable">
'''du'u'''	NU	''predication abstraction''
</tabledata>

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|mental activity}}  {{ind|general-imported|abstractions|with knowing|believing, etc.}}  {{ind|general-imported|propositional attitudes}} There are some selbri which demand an entire predication as a sumti; they make claims about some predication considered as a whole. Logicians call these the 
“propositional attitudes”, and they include (in English) things like knowing, believing, learning, seeing, hearing, and the like. Consider the English sentence:

{{dsp|example-random-id-7N2q}}
{{judri|c11e7d1}}
{{ind|example|Frank is a fool|example}}
{{ind|example|know|example}} 
:''I know that Frank is a fool.''

How's that in Lojban? Let us try:

{{dsp|example-random-id-brpf}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-brpf}}
{{judri|c11e7d2}}
:'''mi djuno le nu la frank. cu bebna [kei]'''
:''I know the event of Frank being a fool.''

{{ind|general-imported|mental activity}} Not quite right. Events are actually or potentially physical, and can't be contained inside one's mind, except for events of thinking, feeling, and the like; 
{{linker|example-random-id-brpf}} comes close to claiming that Frank's being-a-fool is purely a mental activity on the part of the speaker. (In fact, 

{{linker|example-random-id-brpf}} is an instance of improperly marked 
“sumti raising”, a concept discussed further in 

[[#section-sumti-raising|this section]]).

Try again:

{{dsp|example-random-id-oCgP}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-oCgP}}
{{judri|c11e7d3}}
:'''mi djuno le jei la frank. cu bebna [kei]'''
:''I know the truth-value of Frank being a fool.''

Closer. 
{{linker|example-random-id-oCgP}} says that I know whether or not Frank is a fool, but doesn't say that he is one, as {{linker|example-random-id-7N2q}} does. To catch that nuance, we must say:

{{dsp|example-random-id-6p1K}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-6p1K}}
{{judri|c11e7d4}}
:'''mi djuno le du'u la frank. cu bebna [kei]'''
:''I know the predication that Frank is a fool.''

Now we have it. Note that the implied assertion “Frank is a fool” is not a property of {{jbo|le du'u}} abstraction, but of {{vla|djuno}}; we can only know what is in fact true. (As a result, 
{{vla|djuno}} like {{vla|jei}} has a place for epistemology, which specifies how we know.) {{linker|example-random-id-eYiD}} has no such implied assertion:

{{dsp|example-random-id-eYiD}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-eYiD}}
{{judri|c11e7d5}}
:'''mi kucli le du'u la frank. cu bebna [kei]'''
:''I am curious about whether Frank is a fool.''

{{ind|general-imported|curious}} and here 
{{vla|du'u}} could probably be replaced by 
{{vla|jei}} without much change in meaning:

{{dsp|example-random-id-h4De}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-h4De}}
{{judri|c11e7d6}}
{{ind|example|Frank is a fool|example}}
{{ind|example|curious|example}}  
:'''mi kucli le jei la frank. cu bebna [kei]'''
:''I am curious about how true it is that Frank is a fool.''

{{ind|general-imported|truth-value abstractions|place structure}} As a matter of convenience rather than logical necessity, 
{{vla|du'u}} has been given an x2 place, which is a sentence (piece of language) expressing the bridi:

{{vla|du'u}} :''x1 is the predication (the bridi), expressed in sentence x2''

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|speaking|writing, etc.}}  {{ind|general-imported|se du'u}}  {{ind|general-imported|linguistic behavior}} and 
:{{jbo|le se du'u ...}} is very useful in filling places of selbri which refer to speaking, writing, or other linguistic behavior regarding bridi:

{{dsp|example-random-id-hzd8}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-hzd8}}
{{judri|c11e7d7}}
:'''la djan. cusku le se du'u la djordj. klama le zarci [kei]'''
:<code>John expresses the sentence-expressing-that George goes-to the store</code>
:''John says that George goes to the store.''

{{ind|general-imported|quotation|contrasted with sentence abstraction}}  {{ind|general-imported|abstraction of sentences|contrasted with quotation}} 
{{linker|example-random-id-hzd8}} differs from

{{dsp|example-random-id-AX2I}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-AX2I}}
{{judri|c11e7d8}}
:'''la djan cusku lu la djordj. klama le zarci li'u'''
:<code>John expresses, quote, George goes to the store, unquote.</code>
:''John says “George goes to the store”.''

because 
{{linker|example-random-id-AX2I}} claims that John actually said the quoted words, whereas 
{{linker|example-random-id-hzd8}} claims only that he said some words or other which were to the same purpose.

:{{jbo|le se du'u}} is much the same as 
:{{jbo|lu'e le du'u}}, a symbol for the predication, but 
:{{jbo|se du'u}} can be used as a selbri, whereas 
{{vla|lu'e}} is ungrammatical in a selbri. (See [[#section-sumti-qualifiers|this section]] for a discussion of 
{{vla|lu'e}}.)

{{judri|section-indirect-questions}}
==Indirect questions==
The following cmavo is discussed in this section:

<tabledata class="wikitable">
'''kau'''	UI	''indirect question marker''
</tabledata>

There is an alternative type of sentence involving 
{{vla|du'u}} and a selbri expressing a propositional attitude. In addition to sentences like

{{dsp|example-random-id-Fpid}}
{{judri|c11e8d1}}
I know that John went to the store.

we can also say things like

{{dsp|example-random-id-N4Ja}}
{{judri|c11e8d2}}
{{ind|example|know who|example}}
I know who went to the store.

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|with wonder|doubt, etc.}} This form is called an 
“indirect question” in English because the embedded English sentence is a question: 

“Who went to the store?” A person who says 
{{linker|example-random-id-N4Ja}} is claiming to know the answer to this question. Indirect questions can occur with many other English verbs as well: I can wonder, or doubt, or see, or hear, as well as know who went to the store.

To express indirect questions in Lojban, we use a {{jbo|le du'u}} abstraction, but rather than using a question word like 
“who” ( {{vla|ma}} in Lojban), we use any word that will fit grammatically and mark it with the suffix particle 
{{vla|kau}}. This cmavo belongs to selma'o UI, so grammatically it can appear anywhere. The simplest Lojban translation of 

{{linker|example-random-id-N4Ja}} is therefore:

{{dsp|example-random-id-QUxG}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-QUxG}}
{{judri|c11e8d3}}
:'''mi djuno le du'u makau pu klama le zarci'''
:<code>I know the predication-of X [indirect question] [past] going to the store.</code>

{{ind|general-imported|know who|contrasted with know that}}  {{ind|general-imported|indirect questions|&quot;ma kau&quot; contrasted with &quot;la djan. kau&quot;}}  {{ind|general-imported|kau|&quot;ma kau&quot; contrasted with &quot;la djan. kau&quot;}} In 
{{linker|example-random-id-QUxG}}, we have chosen to use 
{{vla|ma}} as the word marked by 
{{vla|kau}}. In fact, any other sumti would have done as well: 

{{vla|zo'e}} or 
{{vla|da}} or even 
:{{jbo|la djan.}}. Using 
:{{jbo|la djan.}} would suggest that it was John who I knew had gone to the store, however:

{{dsp|example-random-id-hmDo}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-hmDo}}
{{judri|c11e8d4}}
:'''mi djuno le du'u la djan. kau pu klama le zarci'''
:<code>I know the predication-of/fact-that John [indirect question] [past] going to the store.</code>
:''I know who went to the store, namely John.''
:''I know that it was John who went to the store.''

Using one of the indefinite pro-sumti such as 

{{vla|ma}}, 
{{vla|zo'e}}, or 
{{vla|da}} does not suggest any particular value.

Why does Lojban require the 
{{vla|kau}} marker, rather than using 

{{vla|ma}} as English and Chinese and many other languages do? Because 
{{vla|ma}} always signals a direct question, and so

{{dsp|example-random-id-5WU4}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-5WU4}}
{{judri|c11e8d5}}
:'''mi djuno le du'u ma pu klama le zarci'''
:<code>I know the predication-of [what sumti?] [past] goes-to the store</code>

means

{{dsp|example-random-id-LDrc}}
{{judri|c11e8d6}}
Who is it that I know goes to the store?

{{ind|general-imported|indirect questions without &quot;kau&quot;}}  {{ind|general-imported|indirect question involving sumti}} It is actually not necessary to use 
:{{jbo|le du'u}} and 
{{vla|kau}} at all if the indirect question involves a sumti; there is generally a paraphrase of the type:

{{dsp|example-random-id-b6VT}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-b6VT}}
{{judri|c11e8d7}}
:'''mi djuno fi le pu klama be le zarci'''
:<code>I know about the [past] goer to-the store.</code>
:''I know something about the one who went to the store (namely, his identity).''

because the x3 place of 
{{vla|djuno}} is the subject of knowledge, as opposed to the fact that is known. But when the questioned point is not a sumti, but (say) a logical connection, then there is no good alternative to 
{{vla|kau}}:

{{dsp|example-random-id-2nIX}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-2nIX}}
{{judri|c11e8d8}}
:'''mi ba zgana le du'u la djan. jikau la djordj. cu zvati le panka'''
:<code>I [future] observe the predication-of/fact-that John [connective indirect question] George is-at the park.</code>
:''I will see whether John or George (or both) is at the park.''

In addition, 
{{linker|example-random-id-b6VT}} is only a loose paraphrase of 
{{linker|example-random-id-QUxG}}, because it is left to the listener's insight to realize that what is known about the goer-to-the-store is his identity rather than some other of his attributes.

{{judri|section-minor-abstractions}}
==Minor abstraction types==
The following cmavo are discussed in this section:

<tabledata class="wikitable">
'''li'i'''	NU	''experience abstractor''
'''si'o'''	NU	''concept abstractor''
'''su'u'''	NU	''general abstractor''
</tabledata>

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|experience}}  {{ind|general-imported|experience abstraction}}  {{ind|general-imported|experience abstractor}} There are three more abstractors in Lojban, all of them little used so far. The abstractor 
{{vla|li'i}} expresses experience:

{{dsp|example-random-id-FS6r}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-FS6r}}
{{judri|c11e9d1}}
:'''mi morji le li'i mi verba'''
:<code>I remember the experience-of (my being-a-child)</code>

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|concept}}  {{ind|general-imported|abstractions|idea}}  {{ind|general-imported|concept abstraction}}  {{ind|general-imported|idea abstraction}}  {{ind|general-imported|concept abstractor}} The abstractor 
{{vla|si'o}} expresses a mental image, a concept, an idea:

{{dsp|example-random-id-Yh42}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-Yh42}}
{{judri|c11e9d2}}
:'''mi nelci le si'o la lojban. cu mulno'''
:<code>I enjoy the concept-of Lojban being-complete.</code>

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|vague}}  {{ind|general-imported|vague abstraction}}  {{ind|general-imported|vague abstractor}} Finally, the abstractor 
{{vla|su'u}} is a vague abstractor, whose meaning must be grasped from context:

{{dsp|example-random-id-ycKt}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-ycKt}}
{{judri|c11e9d3}}
{{ind|example|mice|example}}
:'''ko zgana le su'u le ci smacu cu bajra'''
:<code>you [imperative] observe the abstract-nature-of the three mice running</code>
:''See how the three mice run!''

{{ind|general-imported|experience abstractions|place structure}} All three of these abstractors have an x2 place. An experience requires an experiencer, so the place structure of 
{{vla|li'i}} is:

{{vla|li'i}} :''x1 is the experience of (the bridi) as experienced by x2''

{{ind|general-imported|idea abstractions|place structure}}  {{ind|general-imported|concept abstractions|place structure}} Similarly, an idea requires a mind to hold it, so the place structure of 
{{vla|si'o}} is:

{{vla|si'o}} :''x1 is the idea/concept of (the bridi) in the mind of x2''

{{ind|general-imported|vague abstractions|place structure}} Finally, there needs to be some way of specifying just what sort of abstraction 
{{vla|su'u}} is representing, so its place structure is:

{{vla|su'u}} :''x1 is an abstract nature of (the bridi) of type x2''

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|creating new types}}  {{ind|general-imported|template}} The x2 place of 
{{vla|su'u}} allows it to serve as a substitute for any of the other abstractors, or as a template for creating new ones. For example,

{{dsp|example-random-id-FnNR}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-FnNR}}
{{judri|c11e9d4}}
:'''le nu mi klama'''
:<code>the event-of my going</code>

can be paraphrased as

{{dsp|example-random-id-zvfX}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-zvfX}}
{{judri|c11e9d5}}
:'''le su'u mi klama kei be lo fasnu'''
:<code>the abstract-nature-of (my going) of-type an event</code>

and there is a book whose title might be rendered in Lojban as:

{{dsp|example-random-id-5Kw7}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-5Kw7}}
{{judri|c11e9d6}}
{{ind|example|bicycle race|example}}
{{ind|example|Jesus|example}}  
{{ind|general-imported|intersect}}
{{ind|general-imported|Jesus}} 
:'''le su'u la .iecuas. kuctai selcatra kei be lo sa'ordzifa'a ke nalmatma'e sutyterjvi'''
:<code>the abstract-nature-of (Jesus is-an-intersect-shape type-of-killed-one) of-type a slope-low-direction type-of non-motor-vehicle speed-competition</code>
:''The Crucifixion of Jesus Considered As A Downhill Bicycle Race''

Note the importance of using 
{{vla|kei}} after 
{{vla|su'u}} when the x2 of 
{{vla|su'u}} (or any other abstractor) is being specified; otherwise, the {{jbo|be lo}} ends up inside the abstraction bridi.

{{judri|section-sumti-raising}}
==Lojban sumti raising==

{{ind|general-imported|abstraction conversion}} The following cmavo are discussed in this section:

<tabledata class="wikitable">
'''tu'a'''	LAhE	''an abstraction involving''
'''jai'''	JAI	''abstraction conversion''
</tabledata>

{{ind|general-imported|abstract description}} It is sometimes inconvenient, in a situation where an abstract description is logically required, to express the abstraction. In English we can say:

{{dsp|example-random-id-BYp8}}
{{judri|c11e10d1}}
I try to open the door.

which in Lojban is:

{{dsp|example-random-id-1WER}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-1WER}}
{{judri|c11e10d2}}
:'''mi troci le nu [mi] gasnu le nu le vorme cu karbi'o'''
:<code>I try the event-of (I am-agent-in the event-of (the door open-becomes)).</code>

which has an abstract description within an abstract description, quite a complex structure. In English (but not in all other languages), we may also say:

{{dsp|example-random-id-K14X}}
{{judri|c11e10d3}}
{{ind|example|try the door|example}}
I try the door.

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|simplification to sumti with tu'a}} where it is understood that what I try is actually not the door itself, but the act of opening it. The same simplification can be done in Lojban, but it must be marked explicitly using a cmavo. The relevant cmavo is 
{{vla|tu'a}}, which belongs to selma'o LAhE. The Lojban equivalent of 
{{linker|example-random-id-K14X}} is:

{{dsp|example-random-id-gabC}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-gabC}}
{{judri|c11e10d4}}
:'''mi troci tu'a le vorme'''
:<code>I try some-action-to-do-with the door.</code>

{{ind|general-imported|intermediate abstraction}} The term “sumti-raising”, as in the title of this section, signifies that a sumti which logically belongs within an abstraction (or even within an abstraction which is itself inside an intermediate abstraction) is “raised” to the main bridi level. This transformation from {{linker|example-random-id-1WER}} to {{linker|example-random-id-gabC}} loses information: nothing except convention tells us what the abstraction was.

Using 
{{vla|tu'a}} is a kind of laziness: it makes speaking easier at the possible expense of clarity for the listener. The speaker must be prepared for the listener to respond something like:

{{dsp|example-random-id-mKBy}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-mKBy}}
{{judri|c11e10d5}}
:'''tu'a le vorme lu'u ki'a'''
:<code>something-to-do-with the door [terminator] [confusion!]</code>

which indicates that 
:{{jbo|tu'a le vorme}} cannot be understood. (The terminator for 
{{vla|tu'a}} is 
{{vla|lu'u}}, and is used in 

{{linker|example-random-id-mKBy}} to make clear just what is being questioned: the sumti-raising, rather than the word 
{{vla|vorme}} as such.) An example of a confusing raised sumti might be:

{{dsp|example-random-id-9S5B}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-9S5B}}
{{judri|c11e10d6}}
:'''tu'a la djan. cu cafne'''
:<code>something-to-do-with John frequently-occurs</code>

This must mean that something which John does, or which happens to John, occurs frequently: but without more context there is no way to figure out what. Note that without the 
{{vla|tu'a}}, 
{{linker|example-random-id-9S5B}} would mean that John considered as an event frequently occurs &ndash; in other words, that John has some sort of on-and-off existence! Normally we do not think of people as events in English, but the x1 place of 
{{vla|cafne}} is an event, and if something that does not seem to be an event is put there, the Lojbanic listener will attempt to construe it as one. (Of course, this analysis assumes that 
{{cmevla|djan.}} is the name of a person, and not the name of some event.)

{{ind|general-imported|abstractions|simplification to sumti with jai}}  {{ind|general-imported|abstractions|making concrete}} Logically, a counterpart of some sort is needed to 
{{vla|tu'a}} which transposes an abstract sumti into a concrete one. This is achieved at the selbri level by the cmavo 
{{vla|jai}} (of selma'o JAI). This cmavo has more than one function, discussed in 
[[#section-modal-jai|this section]] and 
[[#section-jai|this section]]; for the purposes of this chapter, it operates as a conversion of selbri, similarly to the cmavo of selma'o SE. This conversion changes

{{dsp|example-random-id-jAdY}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-jAdY}}
{{judri|c11e10d7}}
{{ind|example|cause death|example}}
:'''tu'a mi rinka le nu do morsi'''
:<code>something-to-do-with me causes the event-of you are-dead</code>
:''My action causes your death.''

into {{dsp|example-random-id-R8SN}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-R8SN}}
{{judri|c11e10d8}}
:'''mi jai rinka le nu do morsi'''
:<code>I am-associated-with causing the event-of your death.</code>
:''I cause your death.''

In English, the subject of 
“cause” can either be the actual cause (an event), or else the agent of the cause (a person, typically); not so in Lojban, where the x1 of 
{{vla|rinka}} is always an event. 
{{linker|example-random-id-jAdY}} and 
{{linker|example-random-id-R8SN}} look equally convenient (or inconvenient), but in making descriptions, 
{{linker|example-random-id-R8SN}} can be altered to:

{{dsp|example-random-id-Jt1n}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-Jt1n}}
{{judri|c11e10d9}}
:'''le jai rinka be le nu do morsi'''
:<code>that-which-is associated-with causing (the event-of your death)</code>
:''the one who caused your death''

because {{vla|jai}} modifies the selbri and can be incorporated into the description &ndash; not so for {{vla|tu'a}}.

The weakness of 
{{vla|jai}} used in descriptions in this way is that it does not specify which argument of the implicit abstraction is being raised into the x1 place of the description selbri. One can be more specific by using the modal form of 
{{vla|jai}} explained in 
[[#section-modal-jai|this section]]:

{{dsp|example-random-id-LPbo}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-LPbo}}
{{judri|c11e10d10}}
:'''le jai gau rinka be le nu do morsi'''
:<code>that-which-is agent-in causing (the event-of your death)</code>

{{judri|section-events-and-contours}}
==Event-type abstractors and event contour tenses==
This section is a logical continuation of 
[[#section-event-types|this section]].

{{ind|lojban-word-imported|NU selma'o}} There exists a relationship between the four types of events explained in 
[[#section-event-types|this section]] and the event contour tense cmavo of selma'o ZAhO. The specific cmavo of NU and of ZAhO are mutually interdefining; the ZAhO contours were chosen to fit the needs of the NU event types and vice versa. Event contours are explained in full in 

[[#section-event-contours|this section]], and only summarized here.

The purpose of ZAhO cmavo is to represent the natural portions of an event, such as the beginning, the middle, and the end. They fall into several groups:
* {{ind|general-imported|process abstractions|related tense contours}} The cmavo 
{{vla|pu'o}}, {{vla|ca'o}}, and {{vla|ba'o}} represent spans of time: before an event begins, while it is going on, and after it is over, respectively.
*The cmavo {{vla|co'a}}, {{vla|de'a}}, {{vla|di'a}}, and {{vla|co'u}} represent points of time: the start of an event, the temporary stopping of an event, the resumption of an event after a stop, and the end of an event, respectively. Not all events can have breaks in them, in which case 
{{vla|de'a}} and {{vla|di'a}} do not apply.
*The cmavo {{vla|mo'u}} and {{vla|za'o}} correspond to {{vla|co'u}} and 
{{vla|ba'o}} respectively, in the case of those events which have a natural ending point that may not be the same as the actual ending point: 
{{vla|mo'u}} refers to the natural ending point, and 
{{vla|za'o}} to the time between the natural ending point and the actual ending point (the “excessive” or 
“superfective” part of the event).
*The cmavo 
{{vla|co'i}} represents an entire event considered as a point-event or achievement.

All these cmavo are applicable to events seen as processes and abstracted with 
{{vla|pu'u}}. Only processes have enough internal structure to make all these points and spans of time meaningful.

{{ind|general-imported|state abstractions|related tense contours}} For events seen as states and abstracted with 
{{vla|za'i}}, the meaningful event contours are the spans 

{{vla|pu'o}}, 
{{vla|ca'o}}, and 
{{vla|ba'o}}; the starting and ending points 
{{vla|co'a}} and 
{{vla|co'u}}, and the achievement contour 
{{vla|co'i}}. States do not have natural endings distinct from their actual endings. (It is an open question whether states can be stopped and resumed.)

{{ind|general-imported|activity abstractions|related tense contours}} For events seen as activities and abstracted with 
{{vla|zu'o}}, the meaningful event contours are the spans 

{{vla|pu'o}}, 
{{vla|ca'o}}, and 
{{vla|ba'o}}, and the achievement contour 
{{vla|co'i}}. Because activities are inherently cyclic and repetitive, the beginning and ending points are not well-defined: you do not know whether an activity has truly begun until it begins to repeat.

{{ind|general-imported|achievement abstractions|related tense contours}}  {{ind|general-imported|point-event abstractions|related tense contours}} For events seen as point-events and abstracted with 
{{vla|mu'e}}, the meaningful event contours are the spans 

{{vla|pu'o}} and 
{{vla|ba'o}} but not 
{{vla|ca'o}} (a point-event has no duration), and the achievement contour 
{{vla|co'i}}.

Note that the parts of events are themselves events, and may be treated as such. The points in time may be seen as 
{{vla|mu'e}} point-events; the spans of time may constitute processes or activities. Therefore, Lojban allows us to refer to processes within processes, activities within states, and many other complicated abstract things.

{{judri|section-abstractor-connection}}
==Abstractor connection==
An abstractor may be replaced by two or more abstractors joined by logical or non-logical connectives. Connectives are explained in detail in 
[[#chapter-connectives|this chapter]]. The connection can be expanded to one between two bridi which differ only in abstraction marker. 
{{linker|example-random-id-qFBV}} and 
{{linker|example-random-id-qFdz}} are equivalent in meaning:

{{dsp|example-random-id-qFBV}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qFBV}}
{{judri|c11e12d1}}
:'''le ka la frank. ciska cu xlali .ije le ni la frank. ciska cu xlali'''
:<code>The quality-of Frank's writing is bad, and the quantity of Frank's writing is bad.</code>

{{dsp|example-random-id-qFdz}}{{example|interlinear-gloss-example|example-random-id-qFdz}}
{{judri|c11e12d2}}
:'''le ka je ni la frank. ciska cu xlali'''
:''The quality and quantity of Frank's writing is bad.''

This feature of Lojban has hardly ever been used, and nobody knows what uses it may eventually have.

{{judri|section-summary}}

The following table gives each abstractor, an English gloss for it, a Lojban gismu which is connected with it (more or less remotely: the associations between abstractors and gismu are meant more as memory hooks than for any kind of inference), the rafsi associated with it, and (on the following line) its place structure.</para> <!-- WILL the place structure be on the following line? -->
<tabledata class="wikitable">

{{startchapter|{{#var:uni}}}}{{judri|chapter-lujvo}}
